extracted.intended_audience: researchers and engineers building or studying personalized news recommendation systems (academics, industry practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Survey and catalog of operational features (signals) used by personalized news recommendation systems to decide which news items to surface and how algorithmic 'newsworthiness' is computed. Useful as a reference for model builders, evaluators, and researchers studying algorithmic newsworthiness and personalization trade‑offs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title — Text embedding
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the article title represented as a text embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Content-based feature capturing title semantics for matching to user preferences or topical models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body text — Topic/topic model
rubrics_metrics.description: Represent the article body using topic models or related textual topic features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to infer topical match between article content and user interests; often combined with other content embeddings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category / Topic
rubrics_metrics.description: High-level category or topic label (e.g., politics, sports, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discrete topical signals help coarse-grain user interest and diversify feeds by topic buckets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entities mentioned (NER on people, places, orgs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Named entities extracted from the article (people, places, organizations) via NER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entity-based matching supports interest in specific people/organizations and enables entity-level personalization and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knowledge graph entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Linking content to knowledge-graph entities referenced by the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitates richer semantic matching, entity disambiguation, and related-entity recommendations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sentiment / Emotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Sentiment or emotion signals inferred from the text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to surface content matching users' emotional preferences or to avoid highly negative content; feeds into personalization heuristics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length
rubrics_metrics.description: Article length as a feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May influence predicted dwell time and suitability for short vs. long-session users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reading difficulty
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimated reading difficulty or complexity of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches content complexity to user reading ability or preference (e.g., simple summaries vs. in-depth reporting).

rubrics_metrics.name: Image presence and quality
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the article contains images and the perceived quality of those images.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Visual signals affect click propensity and perceived attractiveness in the feed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication time
rubrics_metrics.description: Timestamp when the article was published.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Basic recency signal used for freshness and temporal relevance calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decay / freshness score
rubrics_metrics.description: A decayed freshness score reflecting how relevance diminishes over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models apply temporal decay to deprioritize stale content; critical for news where recency matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time-of-day publishing
rubrics_metrics.description: The time of day the article was published as a feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can match article timing to user session patterns or time-sensitive interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending velocity
rubrics_metrics.description: Velocity or rate at which an article is gaining attention (trendiness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to surface rapidly rising stories; complements absolute recency with momentum signals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click-through rate (CTR) — historical
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical click-through rate for the article (or similar items).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary engagement signal predicting likelihood of user click; commonly used in ranking models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dwell time — reading depth
rubrics_metrics.description: Measured or predicted dwell time indicating reading depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stronger engagement proxy than clicks alone; used to infer content quality or user satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scroll depth
rubrics_metrics.description: How far users scroll within the article or feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signal of consumption level; deeper scroll indicates higher engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Share count
rubrics_metrics.description: How often the article was shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social engagement metric that can indicate broader interest or virality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comment count
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of comments on the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proxy for engagement and controversy; may be used to prioritize highly discussed items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Like/reaction count
rubrics_metrics.description: Count of likes or reactions the article received.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Another social engagement signal correlated with perceived popularity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bounce rate (negative signal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fraction of users who leave quickly after clicking (bounce); considered a negative signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High bounce suggests low relevance or unsatisfactory content; used to demote similar items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click history — past articles
rubrics_metrics.description: User's historical clicks on past articles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Core personalization signal for learning preferences and short-/long-term affinities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic affinity
rubrics_metrics.description: Learned affinities of the user to topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to score topical match and prioritize content aligned with user interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source affinity
rubrics_metrics.description: User affinity to particular sources or publishers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accounts for loyalty or trust in specific outlets when ranking items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read time / dwell history
rubrics_metrics.description: Historical per-user read times and dwell behavior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Helps model user engagement depth and predict future dwell time for new items.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic location
rubrics_metrics.description: User geographic location as a personalization feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables geographically relevant recommendations and local-news prioritization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Device type
rubrics_metrics.description: Type of device the user is using (mobile, desktop, tablet).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Device affects session length, preference for long/short pieces, and UI layout considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time of session
rubrics_metrics.description: Temporal context of the current session (time of day/week).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to adapt recommendations to typical session behaviors (e.g., morning commute vs. evening browsing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographics (where available)
rubrics_metrics.description: User demographic attributes (age, gender, etc.) when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be used to personalize content broadly, subject to privacy and fairness constraints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friends' clicks
rubrics_metrics.description: Clicks by friends or social connections on the item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Social proof signal feeding into personalization when social graph is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Friends' shares
rubrics_metrics.description: Shares by friends or connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong social endorsement signal that can increase article ranking for connected users.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trending in social network
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the article is trending on social networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: External social momentum used to boost items that are popular across platforms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic neighbors' interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Interests and behaviors of geographically proximate users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local social signals that can inform geographically-relevant personalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Reputation or perceived trustworthiness of the source/publisher.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to favor high-reputation outlets or to demote low-quality publishers; interacts with editorial goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity of sources represented in a user's feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Feature for measuring or enforcing publisher diversity; relevant to anti-filter-bubble objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source recency (when last good story)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recency of a source producing 'good' stories (when the source last had valuable content).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can influence when to re-surface items from the same publisher or adjust source weighting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher size / brand
rubrics_metrics.description: Publisher size or brand strength as a feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Large/recognized brands may get higher baseline weighting due to familiarity and trust.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topic diversity within feed
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of topic diversity included within a user's feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit diversity/serendipity feature to avoid monotonous topical streams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source diversity within feed
rubrics_metrics.description: Degree of source diversity in the feed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engineered signal to ensure multiple outlets are represented and reduce bias from single-source dominance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anti-filter-bubble mechanics
rubrics_metrics.description: Mechanisms intentionally designed to counteract filter bubbles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithmic interventions (e.g., injecting diverse items) to increase exposure to differing viewpoints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Novelty — seen vs. unseen
rubrics_metrics.description: Novelty measured as whether content is seen or unseen by the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to surface new information and balance exploitation of known preferences with exploration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted personal relevance ≠ traditional news values
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms prioritize predicted personal relevance, which can differ from traditional journalistic news values.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights that personalization operationalizes newsworthiness differently from editorial criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Predicted engagement dominates
rubrics_metrics.description: Predicted engagement (clicks, dwell) often dominates ranking decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates a bias toward what will attract attention rather than necessarily what is most informationally important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recency highly weighted
rubrics_metrics.description: Recency is frequently given a high weight in ranking news items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leads systems to prioritize the newest items, which can advantage breaking news over sustained relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical match over significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithms tend to favor topical matches with user interests rather than objective significance of a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May surface less important but topically aligned items over more significant but off-topic reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social proof (peers liked it)
rubrics_metrics.description: Social proof—signals that peers liked or engaged with an item—affects ranking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer behavior can amplify items within social and friendship graphs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic proximity (when known)
rubrics_metrics.description: Geographic proximity between user and event/place is used as a relevance signal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Local proximity often increases ranking for geographically relevant stories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Source familiarity / loyalty
rubrics_metrics.description: Familiarity with and loyalty to sources influences personalization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Users returning to known sources can bias recommendation distributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity is engineered, not organic
rubrics_metrics.description: Diversity present in feeds is typically engineered by algorithms rather than emergent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implies that diversity metrics need explicit modeling and intervention rather than relying on organic exposure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personalization vs. shared public information (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade-off between tailoring to individual tastes and maintaining shared public information exposure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designers must balance individualized relevance with the civic role of news in creating shared knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engagement maximization vs. accuracy (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between optimizing for engagement and ensuring factual accuracy or quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: High-engagement signals can favor sensational or misleading content; systems should consider verification/accuracy features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filter bubbles vs. exposure to diverse views (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trade-off between creating comfortable personalized streams and exposing users to diverse viewpoints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mitigation requires explicit diversity/serendipity features and evaluation metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Click prediction vs. quality (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Tension between optimizing for click prediction metrics and promoting high-quality journalism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Models should include quality signals (e.g., dwell, source reputation) to counter pure click-optimization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Algorithmic newsworthiness diverges from editorial newsworthiness (tension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Algorithmic measures of newsworthiness often diverge from traditional editorial judgments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognition of this divergence suggests hybrid approaches or editorial constraints may be necessary.
